1.overview: The chapter identifies Jeremiah of Anathoth and dates his prophetic ministry from Josiah’s reign through Jerusalem’s exile under Zedekiah, as the LORD appoints him prophet to the nations and equips him to speak. Through visions of an almond branch and a boiling pot, the LORD announces judgment from the north against Judah for its idolatry and promises to deliver Jeremiah despite opposition.

sections.heading: Visions of Judgment from the North

2.overview: The LORD recalls Israel’s early devotion, then accuses its people and leaders of abandoning him for idols despite his deliverance and provision. He describes the resulting devastation, condemns Judah’s idolatry and injustice, and warns that reliance on Egypt and Assyria will fail.

3.overview: The LORD condemns Israel’s and Judah’s idolatry, declaring Judah’s pretense worse than Israel’s open unfaithfulness. He calls Israel to return, promises restoration in Zion and the reunion of Israel and Judah, and concludes with Israel’s confession of sin and appeal for mercy.

sections.heading: Call to Return and Promise of Restoration

4.overview: The LORD calls Israel and Judah to return, reform their hearts, and live in truth, while warning that an invading force from the north will bring judgment on Jerusalem. Jeremiah laments the coming devastation as the land is laid waste, its people flee, and Daughter Zion cries out before her attackers.

sections.heading: Jeremiah’s Lament and the Desolate Land

5.overview: The LORD finds no one in Jerusalem who acts justly or seeks truth, and Jeremiah describes the people’s hardened rebellion, idolatry, and unfaithfulness. The LORD announces invasion and exile while sparing a remnant, then condemns the people’s disregard for him, social injustice, and acceptance of false prophets and self-appointed priests.

6.overview: Jeremiah warns Benjamin and Jerusalem of an invading army from the north and describes the city’s oppression, violence, and coming destruction. The people reject the LORD’s word, the ancient paths, and the warnings of watchmen, while corrupt leaders offer false assurances; the chapter ends with the enemy’s approach and Judah’s failed refining.

sections.heading: The Northern Army and Rejected Silver

7.overview: Jeremiah proclaims at the temple gate that Judah’s safety depends not on the temple but on just conduct, care for the vulnerable, and exclusive worship of the LORD; he warns that continued violence and idolatry will bring judgment like Shiloh’s. The LORD rejects the people’s sacrifices and recounts their refusal to obey the prophets, then condemns the idols in the temple and the child sacrifices at Topheth, foretelling slaughter and the end of celebration in Judah and Jerusalem.

sections.heading: Judgment for Worship of the Queen of Heaven

8.overview: The LORD announces the exposure of Judah’s graves and condemns Jerusalem’s persistent refusal to repent, false claims of wisdom, and deceitful assurances of peace. He declares judgment through failed harvests, enemy invasion, and affliction, while Jeremiah voices grief over the people’s devastation and lack of healing.

sections.heading: Jeremiah’s Grief and the People’s Wound

9.overview: Jeremiah laments Judah’s deceit and faithlessness as the LORD announces punishment, Jerusalem’s desolation, and the people’s scattering. The chapter calls for mourning, rejects boasting in wisdom, strength, or wealth, and warns that circumcision of the flesh cannot protect those uncircumcised in heart.

sections.heading: True Boasting and Circumcision of the Heart

10.overview: The LORD warns Israel against the customs and idols of the nations, contrasting powerless images with the living God, King and Creator. He announces the displacement of the land’s inhabitants and devastation from the north, while the speaker laments Judah’s ruin and asks the LORD for just correction and judgment on the nations.

11.overview: The LORD reminds Jeremiah to proclaim the covenant to Judah and Jerusalem, recounts their persistent disobedience and idolatry, and announces disaster from which neither the people nor their gods can deliver them. The LORD forbids Jeremiah to intercede, describes Judah’s destruction, and answers the plot against Jeremiah by declaring judgment on the men of Anathoth who seek his life.

12.overview: Jeremiah questions why the wicked prosper, affirms that the LORD knows his heart, and asks how long the land will suffer for its people’s evil; the LORD warns Jeremiah about greater trials and betrayal by his family. The LORD describes the devastation of his inheritance by enemies and declares that he will uproot hostile nations, later show them compassion if they learn his people’s ways, and destroy any nation that refuses to obey.

sections.heading: Warning of Greater Trials and Betrayal
The Desolation of the LORD’s Inheritance
Uprooting and Restoration of the Nations

13.overview: Jeremiah acts out the sign of a ruined linen loincloth, which the LORD uses to declare that Judah and Jerusalem have become useless through pride, disobedience, and worship of other gods; he also warns that their leaders and people will be filled with drunkenness and destroyed. The chapter calls for attention to the LORD’s warning, announces the king and queen mother’s humiliation and Judah’s exile, and attributes Jerusalem’s coming disgrace to its entrenched sin and false worship.

14.overview: Jeremiah describes the drought devastating Judah and the people’s pleas for the LORD to act despite their sins. The LORD rejects prayer and offerings, condemns the prophets who promise peace, and Jeremiah voices the people’s confession and appeal to the LORD’s covenant.

15.overview: The LORD rejects even hypothetical intercession by Moses and Samuel, assigns Judah death, sword, famine, and captivity, and links Jerusalem’s devastation to Manasseh’s deeds. Jeremiah laments his conflict and suffering, recalls his devotion to the LORD’s words, and receives a promise of restoration and protection amid further judgment on Judah.

sections.heading: Jeremiah’s Plea and the LORD’s Promise

16.overview: The LORD forbids Jeremiah to marry, mourn, or feast in Judah as signs that disease, violence, exile, and the loss of communal joy are coming. He explains that judgment follows the people’s idolatry and disobedience, promises their return from exile, and declares that the nations will recognize his power and name.

17.overview: Judah’s idolatry is engraved on its heart and altars, bringing exile, while Jeremiah contrasts trust in the LORD with trust in human strength and declares that the LORD searches the heart. Jeremiah asks the LORD for healing and protection, then delivers a warning at Jerusalem’s gates that Sabbath observance will bring the city’s continued life, while disobedience will bring its destruction by fire.

sections.heading: The Sabbath Warning at Jerusalem’s Gates

18.overview: The LORD sends Jeremiah to a potter’s house, then uses the potter’s reshaping of flawed clay to explain how he may change his purposes for Israel and other nations in response to their conduct; Judah and Jerusalem are warned to turn from evil, but they reject the warning. The LORD condemns Israel’s idolatry and announces disaster, while Jeremiah’s opponents plot against him and he asks the LORD to judge them.

19.overview: The LORD sends Jeremiah with Judah’s elders and priests to the Valley of Ben-hinnom, where he announces Jerusalem’s coming devastation because its people have abandoned the LORD, worshiped other gods, and shed innocent blood. Jeremiah shatters a clay jar as a sign that Judah and Jerusalem will be irreparably broken, then proclaims in the temple courtyard that disaster will come on the city and surrounding villages because the people refuse to heed the LORD’s words.

sections.heading: The Shattered Jar as a Sign

20.overview: Pashhur has Jeremiah beaten and confined, but Jeremiah renames him Magor-missabib and announces captivity for Pashhur, his household, and Judah. Jeremiah laments the ridicule and danger surrounding his prophetic work, affirms the LORD’s support and rescue, then curses the day of his birth and grieves over his life of trouble and shame.

sections.heading: Jeremiah’s lament and confidence in the LORD
Jeremiah curses the day of his birth

21.overview: Zedekiah sends Pashhur and Zephaniah to ask Jeremiah to seek the LORD’s help against Nebuchadnezzar, but Jeremiah announces that Jerusalem will fall and its survivors will be handed over to Babylon. He sets before the people a choice between death in the besieged city and life through surrender, then calls the house of David to administer justice and warns that judgment will consume its stronghold.

sections.heading: The Way of Life and Death
Warning to the House of David

22.overview: Jeremiah delivers the LORD’s warning to Judah’s king and officials: justice for the vulnerable will preserve the royal house, but disobedience will bring Jerusalem’s desolation. He announces the exile of Shallum, the dishonorable death of Jehoiakim, and the removal of Coniah and the end of his descendants’ rule in Judah.

23.overview: The LORD condemns Israel’s negligent shepherds, promises to gather the scattered people and raise a righteous Branch from David, and foretells their return to the land. He denounces prophets who speak lies and false assurances, declares that his word exposes and judges them, and announces punishment for those who misuse the phrase “the burden of the LORD.”

sections.heading: Negligent shepherds and the righteous Branch
The LORD’s word against deceptive prophecy
Misuse of “the burden of the LORD”

24.overview: After Jeconiah and other Judeans are taken to Babylon, Jeremiah sees two baskets of figs beside the temple. The LORD identifies the good figs with the exiles whom he will restore and the bad figs with Zedekiah, his officials, and the remaining Judeans, whom he will judge.

sections.heading: The Good Figs and the Exiles

25.overview: Jeremiah recounts Judah’s rejection of repeated prophetic warnings and announces its devastation under Nebuchadnezzar, seventy years of service to Babylon, and Babylon’s later punishment. He gives the nations the cup of the LORD’s wrath and proclaims judgment across the earth, including the slaughter of its leaders and people.

sections.heading: Judah’s judgment and Babylon’s seventy years
The cup of wrath for the nations
The LORD’s judgment across the earth

26.overview: At the beginning of Jehoiakim’s reign, the LORD sends Jeremiah to warn Judah that the temple and Jerusalem will become like Shiloh unless the people listen; priests and prophets demand his death, but officials and people acquit him after his defense. Judah’s elders cite Micah’s similar prophecy and Hezekiah’s response, while Jehoiakim has Uriah brought back from Egypt and executed, and Ahikam protects Jeremiah.

27.overview: The LORD commands Jeremiah to wear a yoke and tell the envoys of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre, and Sidon that Nebuchadnezzar will rule the nations, while those who resist him face judgment and those who submit remain in their lands. Jeremiah gives the same warning to Zedekiah, the priests, and the people, rejecting false promises of deliverance and declaring that the remaining temple and royal objects will be taken to Babylon until the LORD restores them.

28.overview: Hananiah prophesies in the temple that the LORD will break Babylon’s yoke within two years and restore the temple articles and exiles, while Jeremiah says that peace is confirmed only when prophecy comes true. After Hananiah breaks Jeremiah’s wooden yoke and repeats his prediction, the LORD declares that an iron yoke will bind the nations to Nebuchadnezzar, condemns Hananiah for false prophecy, and announces his death that year.

sections.heading: The Iron Yoke and Hananiah’s Death

29.overview: Jeremiah sends a letter to the Judean exiles in Babylon, instructing them to settle there and promising their eventual restoration after seventy years while warning them against false prophets. The LORD announces judgment on those remaining in Jerusalem and on the false prophets Ahab, Zedekiah, and Shemaiah, whose claims oppose Jeremiah’s message.

sections.heading: Judgment on Jerusalem and False Prophets

30.overview: The LORD tells Jeremiah to record his promise to restore Israel and Judah, deliver Jacob from distress, free the people from foreign rule, and raise up David as their king. He describes Zion’s grievous wounds and punishment, then promises healing, rebuilding, renewed honor, and a ruler from the people while declaring judgment on the wicked.

31.overview: The LORD promises to restore Israel and Judah, gathering the exiles, turning mourning to joy, and renewing the land. He announces a new covenant written on the people’s hearts, assures Israel’s lasting place as a nation, and promises Jerusalem’s rebuilding and holiness.

32.overview: While Jerusalem is under siege and Jeremiah is imprisoned for prophesying its capture, he buys his cousin Hanamel’s field at Anathoth and has the deeds preserved as a sign that land will again be purchased. In response to Jeremiah’s prayer, the LORD confirms Jerusalem’s judgment for Judah’s idolatry and promises to gather the people, establish an everlasting covenant with them, and restore the land.

33.overview: While Jeremiah is confined, the LORD promises to answer him and to restore Jerusalem and Judah with healing, forgiveness, renewed life, and abundant peace. The LORD promises a righteous Branch from David, enduring roles for David’s line and the Levite priests, and compassion for the descendants of Jacob.

sections.heading: The Righteous Branch and Enduring Promises

34.overview: During the Babylonian siege of Jerusalem, Jeremiah tells Zedekiah that the city will fall and he will be taken to Babylon, where he will die in peace. After Jerusalem’s people free their Hebrew slaves and then enslave them again, the LORD condemns their broken covenant and declares that Babylon will return to destroy the city and devastate Judah.

sections.heading: The people free and re-enslave Hebrew slaves
The covenant penalty and Babylon’s return

35.overview: During Jehoiakim’s reign, Jeremiah brings the Rechabites to a chamber in the temple and offers them wine, but they refuse, citing their forefather Jonadab’s commands. The LORD contrasts their obedience with Judah’s refusal to heed his words, announces disaster for Judah and Jerusalem, and promises that Jonadab’s line will continue to serve before him.

sections.heading: Jeremiah Brings the Rechabites to the Temple
The Rechabites Explain Their Ancestral Commands

36.overview: In Jehoiakim’s reign, Jeremiah dictates the LORD’s warnings to Baruch, who reads the scroll to the people and then to Judah’s officials. Jehoiakim burns the scroll and orders Jeremiah and Baruch seized, but the LORD has them hidden, directs Jeremiah to produce another scroll, and declares judgment on the king and his house.

37.overview: Zedekiah and Judah’s leaders reject Jeremiah’s words, though Zedekiah asks him to pray, and the Chaldeans withdraw from Jerusalem when Pharaoh’s army approaches. The LORD says the Chaldeans will return and capture the city; Jeremiah is arrested, then tells Zedekiah he will be handed over to Babylon before being moved to the guard’s courtyard.

sections.heading: Zedekiah’s Reign and the Siege’s Pause

38.overview: Officials accuse Jeremiah of weakening Jerusalem and have him thrown into a cistern, but Ebed-melech persuades Zedekiah to order his rescue. In a private meeting, Jeremiah tells Zedekiah that surrender to Babylon will spare him and the city from destruction, while the king conceals their conversation and Jeremiah remains in the courtyard of the guard.

39.overview: Nebuchadnezzar’s army besieges and breaches Jerusalem, and Zedekiah flees, is captured near Jericho, and is blinded after his sons and Judah’s nobles are killed at Riblah. The Chaldeans burn and break down the city, deport many inhabitants while leaving some poor people in Judah, release Jeremiah into Gedaliah’s care, and receive the LORD’s promise to rescue Ebed-melech.

40.overview: Nebuzaradan frees Jeremiah at Ramah, explains that Judah’s disaster fulfills the LORD’s judgment, and offers him the choice to go to Babylon or remain; Jeremiah stays with Gedaliah at Mizpah. Gedaliah welcomes the field commanders and returning Judeans, urges them to live peacefully under Babylonian rule, and rejects Johanan’s warning that Ishmael plans to kill him.

sections.heading: Gedaliah and the Remnant at Mizpah

41.overview: Ishmael son of Nethaniah murders Gedaliah at Mizpah, kills Jews and Chaldeans there, slaughters visiting worshipers, and takes the remaining people captive toward the Ammonites. Johanan son of Kareah and the army commanders recover the captives near Gibeon, while Ishmael escapes and Johanan’s group stays near Bethlehem before planning to flee to Egypt for fear of the Chaldeans.

42.overview: Johanan, the commanders, and the remnant of Judah ask Jeremiah to seek the LORD’s direction and pledge to obey it. After ten days, Jeremiah tells them to remain in Judah for protection and restoration, warns that Egypt will bring sword, famine, and plague, and accuses them of insincerity when they refuse to obey.

sections.heading: The Remnant Seeks the LORD’s Direction
Promise for Those Who Remain in Judah

43.overview: Azariah, Johanan, and the other leaders reject Jeremiah’s warning and take the remnant of Judah, including Jeremiah and Baruch, to Egypt, settling at Tahpanhes. There the LORD tells Jeremiah to bury stones at Pharaoh’s palace as a sign that Nebuchadnezzar will conquer Egypt, strike its people, and destroy its temples and sacred pillars.

44.overview: Jeremiah recounts Judah’s destruction as the result of persistent idolatry and warns the Jews living in Egypt that they too will die by sword or famine, with only a few escaping. The people reject his warning and defend their worship of the Queen of Heaven, while Jeremiah declares that their conduct brought disaster on Judah and foretells their destruction and the downfall of Pharaoh Hophra.

sections.heading: The people defend the Queen of Heaven worship
Jeremiah confirms judgment and its sign

45.overview: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim, Jeremiah delivers the Lord’s message to Baruch, who laments his sorrow, exhaustion, and lack of rest. The Lord announces the destruction of what he has built and planted, warns Baruch not to seek great things for himself, and promises to preserve his life amid disaster.

46.overview: Jeremiah recounts Egypt’s defeat by Nebuchadnezzar at Carchemish, portraying the Egyptian army’s flight and the LORD’s judgment by the Euphrates. He announces Babylon’s coming attack on Egypt and its eventual recovery, then promises Jacob’s return from captivity while affirming that the LORD will discipline Israel.

47.overview: The chapter introduces the LORD’s word to Jeremiah concerning the Philistines, delivered before Pharaoh strikes Gaza, and describes an invading force from the north as a flood that brings terror and destruction. The LORD declares the destruction of the Philistines and their allies, while Gaza and Ashkelon mourn and the LORD’s sword continues against Ashkelon and its coast.

sections.heading: Philistine mourning and the LORD’s sword

48.overview: Jeremiah announces Moab’s devastation, naming its cities and describing its people’s flight, the exile of Chemosh, and the collapse of Moab’s strength. He portrays the judgment as the result of Moab’s pride and mockery of Israel, laments the nation’s loss, and concludes with a promise of restoration in later days.

49.overview: The LORD announces judgment on Ammon for taking Israel’s territory, on Edom and Damascus, and on Kedar and Hazor through Nebuchadnezzar’s campaign. He also declares judgment on Elam, including the scattering of its people, and promises restoration for Ammon and Elam afterward.

sections.heading: Nebuchadnezzar’s campaign against Kedar and Hazor

50.overview: Jeremiah announces Babylon’s capture by a northern alliance and its judgment for plundering Israel and defying the LORD. Israel and Judah seek the LORD, return toward Zion in an everlasting covenant, and receive forgiveness and restoration as the LORD their Redeemer brings Babylon to ruin.

sections.heading: The northern army and Babylon’s fall

51.overview: The LORD announces Babylon’s destruction by the Medes, vindication for Israel and Judah, and Babylon’s lasting desolation, while calling the LORD’s people to flee. Jeremiah gives Seraiah a scroll of the judgment to read in Babylon and sink in the Euphrates as a sign that the city will never rise again.

sections.heading: Babylon’s judgment and the LORD’s sovereignty
The scroll sunk in the Euphrates

52.overview: The chapter recounts Zedekiah’s rebellion, Babylon’s siege and capture of Jerusalem, the destruction of the temple and city, and the deportation of Judah’s people. It concludes with the release and favored treatment of Jehoiachin in Babylon.
